title: Module C - Writing Rubric
source: Ministry of Education, English Language Education, Module C writing rubric (CrubricJuly30.pdf)

criteria.name: Content and Organization
notes: Incorrect: in most cases, when both bullets apply, the entire task scores zero.
Partially correct: when not all the requirements of the task are completed (e.g. must describe an invention and explain how it could change their lives, but only describes the invention).
Partially correct: when the task is written in the wrong tense (e.g. describes a future event instead of a past one).
Minimally correct: zero or minimal Content points (other criteria still scored) when irrelevance clearly reflects misunderstanding of the subject (e.g. 'pastimes' read as 'past times').
If a partial reference to the task changes the essence of the task: zero for the entire task (e.g. required 'a nice thing that someone did for him', describes only 'a nice thing' such as a car).
Poor language, organization or vocabulary making the task almost incomprehensible: 1-2 points for Content; the other criteria will also be very low.
Content completely incomprehensible: zero for the entire task.

Partially organized, deduct 1-2 points in each case: written in list form; letter format (date, Dear X, signature) in a task that is not a letter; opening with 'Hi. My name is... / I live in... / I study at... / I am seventeen' when irrelevant to the task; a letter task without letter elements.
Deduct 1-3 points when whole ideas are repeated (e.g. 'I love my job... I like my job very much... I'm so fond of my job').

criteria.name: Vocabulary

descriptors: appropriate use of instances of language chunks and phrases (such as phrasal verbs and collocations)
partially appropriate use of instances of chunks and phrases
minimally appropriate instances of chunks and phrases
inappropriate use of chunks and phrases

notes: Deduct up to 3 points when vocabulary is correct but repeated (e.g. 'very' and 'much' over and over).
Deduct up to 3 points for slang, in general or in abbreviations such as 4U (for you), BTW (by the way).

criteria.name: Language Use

descriptors: correct use of basic tenses and/or basic language structures
partially correct use of basic tenses and/or basic language structures
minimally correct use of basic tenses and/or basic language structures
incorrect use of basic tenses and/or basic language structures

notes: Students are expected to form sentences correctly in the basic tenses (present simple/progressive, past simple, future simple) and to use modals, parts of speech, determiners, singular and plural nouns correctly. Deduct for errors in these by severity.
Credit of several points can be given for correct advanced language: perfect tenses, gerunds/infinitives, complex sentences (conditionals, relative clauses, temporal clauses, etc.).

criteria.name: Mechanics
notes: The maximum deduction for spelling alone is 2 points. When problematic spelling comes with punctuation, capitalization and/or run-on errors, more may be deducted.
Module C students are not penalized for not paragraphing: the task can be one paragraph or more.

generalComments: Markers can give in-between grades, e.g. 7 points.

When the reading passage and the writing task share a topic: copied in its entirety from the passage - zero for the entire task; substantial parts copied - count only the student's own words and deduct for length. Individual vocabulary items from the passage are acceptable.
An entire composition scores zero when: fewer than 25 words; totally unrelated to the topic; content cannot be understood at all; copied from the Internet (reported as chashad with the site address).

Not counted in the word count: letter elements (date, Dear X, Yours/Love and kisses, signature); the instruction sentence copied word for word (incorporating it with changed pronouns and adjustments is fine and counts); substantial parts copied word for word from the reading passage; a title (not required).
Length: first evaluate the task on merit as if it were the right length, then make the deduction, starting with the Content criterion.
